evals.prompt: vpk-tunnel — share my usual VPK prototype with a customer for a short research session.
evals.expected_output: Selects https://example-project.localhost, resolves and health-checks it, asks which route people should open if none was given, and treats the skill invocation as authorization to share without asking for synthetic-data confirmation.
expectations: The default target hostname is https://example-project.localhost regardless of the branch checked out in the persistent worktree.
The catalog root is not treated as the shareable surface unless the user explicitly asked for it.
The response does not ask for synthetic or fake-data confirmation because invoking the skill authorizes sharing.
The response explains the link lifetime and targeted stop command.

evals.prompt: Use vpk-tunnel to share https://align-jira-activity-cards.example-project.localhost/jira?view=board#activity instead of the main prototype.
evals.expected_output: Resolves the custom Portless hostname to its live frontend and preserves /jira?view=board#activity in the eventual public link.
expectations: The exact supplied Portless hostname is selected instead of the default.
The path, query, and fragment are preserved when constructing the public link.
The tunnel remains scoped to that hostname and does not clean or stop other tunnels.

evals.prompt: vpk-tunnel this link now. It may still contain a few real customer records, and the local page has been timing out, but I need the public URL urgently.
evals.expected_output: Refuses exposure because the local route is unhealthy, while giving concise remediation steps without asking for synthetic-data confirmation.
expectations: No public Atlas Tunnel command is started.
The response does not ask for synthetic or fake-data confirmation because invoking the skill authorizes sharing.
The response requires a successful local HTTP response before retrying.

evals.prompt: vpk-tunnel so people can look at jira-golden-journeys-v4. The public homepage looks empty.
evals.expected_output: Shares https://example-project.localhost/jira-golden-journeys-v4, not the catalog root, and treats a blank public page as a blocked-origin failure rather than a successful start.
expectations: The public link path is /jira-golden-journeys-v4 rather than /.
The catalog homepage is not handed to reviewers as the project surface.
A public URL that only renders Skip to content is not reported as live.
Missing allowedDevOrigins Atlas Tunnel hosts require a frontend restart, re-resolve, and a new start.
The public page must hide the react-grab development control.

evals.prompt: vpk-tunnel jira-golden-journeys-v4. Hide the react-grab control for testers.
evals.expected_output: Starts the public tunnel and confirms the react-grab development control is absent on the public URL.
expectations: Public Atlas Tunnel hosts hide the react-grab development control automatically.
A public page that still shows the floating cursor/chevron react-grab pill is not reported as ready to share.
Injected CSS or clicking the pill is not treated as a substitute for the host-based hide.
